exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Probability of a Union Using the Addition Law

question.text: Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are two events such that $P(A)=0.5,$ $P(B)=0.65,$ and $P(A\cap B)=0.35,$ find $P(A\cup B).$
question.explanation:
The addition law for probability states that

\[ P(A\cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A\cap B). \]

So, to calculate $P(A\cup B),$ we apply the addition law: \[ \begin{align*} P(A\cup B) &= P(A) + P(B) - P(A\cap B)\\[5pt] &= 0.5 + 0.65 - 0.35 \\[5pt] &= 0.8 \end{align*} \]
